title: OIL FOR A LAMP THAT NEVER GOES OUT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
The LORD said to Moses, "Command the Israelites to bring you clear oil
of pressed olives for the light so that the lamps may be kept burning
continually" - Lev 24:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The lamps inside the tabernacle were to burn continually, and the oil
came from the people. Ordinary families pressed their olives and
carried the oil to the sanctuary so that the light of God's house would
not go out.

Notice how humble the contribution was. Nobody's name was recorded on
the jar. The oil was poured in, consumed, and forgotten. Yet without it
the lamps would have died.

Dear friend, much of the most important work in God's kingdom looks
exactly like that. The woman who prays for her children at four in the
morning. The man who quietly pays a poorer family's school fees. The
volunteer who arranges chairs before anyone arrives. Nobody sees the
oil. Everybody sees the light.

Paul reminds us that God is not unjust; He will not forget your work
and the love you have shown Him as you have helped His people (Heb
6:10). Jesus spoke of a Father who sees what is done in secret and
rewards it (Matt 6:4).

Do not despise your small contribution. The light in your church, your
family, your fellowship group is being sustained partly by people whose
names will never be announced.

Keep bringing the oil.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What quiet, unseen contribution am I making to God's work?
2. Have I grown discouraged because nobody notices?
3. Whose faithful, hidden service should I thank this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that no small offering is wasted with You. Help me
serve faithfully even when nobody notices, and make me quick to
encourage those who serve unseen. Amen.
